scenes.headline: How a PyTorch model becomes one GPU kernel
scenes.sub: MegaBake compiles a whole decode step into a single launch.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tenon! MegaBake takes a PyTorch model and bakes a whole decode step into one GPU kernel. Here's how that works.

scenes.text: A small model at batch one spends most of a token launching kernels. Launch once, and let resident blocks walk a table of every step.
scenes.say: A small model at batch one spends most of each token launching kernels. So launch once, and let blocks that never exit walk a table of every step.

scenes.title: From a graph to one persistent kernel

steps.say: Dynamo captures the model, and Inductor's own passes clean up the graph. MegaBake takes that graph and stops Inductor there.
It groups the operations into regions, picks a body for each, and writes every step of the token as a row in one table.
One kernel launches sixty blocks, one per processor, and they all walk the same table.
Each row names a body: a matrix tile, a norm, or attention. A grid barrier closes each interval before the next rows begin.

left.title: Per-op kernels
items: Host time dominates at batch one
Each kernel ramps up and drains
left.say: The usual way launches hundreds of kernels per token, and at batch one the host's launch time dwarfs the work.

right.title: One megakernel
items: Small steps recomputed by every block
right.say: MegaBake launches once. Blocks synchronize with barriers, and tiny steps like norms are recomputed by every block, so they need no barrier of their own.

scenes.title: SmolLM-135M decode, microseconds
scenes.say: The repo's own numbers. End to end, the single launch wins by about five times. But on GPU time alone, Inductor's kernels are slightly faster, and its baseline ran without CUDA graphs.

scenes.text: The win today is launch overhead. A megakernel beats CUDA graphs only once it overlaps work across barriers.
scenes.say: So the win today is launch overhead. To beat CUDA graphs too, a megakernel has to overlap work across its barriers, and that is next on the roadmap.

recap: FX graph in, one CuTe kernel out
Sixty blocks walk a phase table
Fast end to end, not on GPU
scenes.say: Graph in, one kernel out. Sixty blocks walk a table. Faster end to end, not yet on the GPU.
